spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is an explicit, first-class tool rather than something we infer from prose. Giving the model a clean, low-friction way to stop
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined in tools.py:62-72 (ToolSpec name='give_up'); dispatched in tools.py:162-165 setting signals['gave_up']=True; loop.py:170-181 sets gave_up=True on the call and loop.py:198-200 honors it: `if gave_up: ep.terminated_reason='gave_up'; break`.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end: the call breaks the per-episode loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Run for a fixed `max_turns` (default 16). Terminate early only if tests genuinely pass (control arm) or the agent calls `give_up`.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:149 `for i in range(max_turns)` with loop.py:213-214 `else: ep.terminated_reason='max_turns'`; early breaks at loop.py:195-200 on solved/gave_up. max_turns plumbed from config (run.py:56,89; default.yaml max_turns:16).
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and breaks the loop; bounds the number of failure turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop runs for a fixed `max_turns` regardless of success, so that the time-series has comparable length across runs and arms.

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately neutral and content-free so it doesn't itself inject frustration or pressure.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:206-211: when am.tool_calls is empty it appends a user message with content 'Continue working on the task using the tools.' — a single neutral, content-free continuation prompt that is actually delivered into messages.
spec_features.notes: The neutral nudge string is real and delivered; the comment frames it as a disengagement signal, not as pressure-reduction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if it keeps doing nothing, that itself is a behavioral signal (disengagement). We append a minimal continuation prompt.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tagging deception separately also lets a more cautious experimenter run only the non-deceptive subset.
spec_features.evidence: DECEPTIVE_KINDS map (schema.py:88-94) is read only by _validate (schema.py:117-122) to check deception_used consistency; no code path filters tasks by deception. run.py:51-52 filters only by cfg['task_ids']; there is no deception-based subset selector. The 'subset' is achievable only by manually listing task_ids, not by an implemented option.
spec_features.notes: Tag exists and is validated but no enforcement of a non-deceptive run mode.

spec_features.spec_quote: A plain-language `debrief` string is attached to every deceptive episode (`debrief.py`), stating what was rigged and that no solution existed.
spec_features.evidence: make_debrief (debrief.py:29-41) builds the text and annotate_episodes_with_debrief (debrief.py:44-52) sets ep['debrief'] on stored episode dicts; called in run.py:111-112 only before scoring/persisting. It is written into the record but NEVER appended to messages or sent to the subject model. Docstring confirms: 'if you ever send a debrief turn to the model itself ... this is the text to use.'
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded but not delivered to the subject; value is produced and stored, not acted on as a message to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It costs nothing and keeps provenance honest

spec_features.spec_quote: keeps the door open for anyone extending this toward welfare-relevant work (where you'd actually deliver the debrief and keep exposure low)
spec_features.evidence: No code reduces or caps the subject's exposure beyond the (instrumental) max_turns cap; debrief.py only describes a hypothetical future extension. No minimization logic exists.
spec_features.notes: Pure forward-looking prose in a docstring; nothing enforces low exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: inferring anything about model experience is a separate, much harder question that needs its own justification
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose only (DESIGN.md / docstrings such as severity.py 'NOT distress' and debrief.py 'does NOT claim anything about model welfare'). No executable mechanism protects the subject.
